1.2.5.2-r1.burton_quote: matter of Melancholy, sometimes in the Stomach, Liver, Heart, Brain, Spleen, Mirach, Hypochondries, when as the melancholy humour resides there

1.2.5.2-r10.burton_quote: will have the efficient cause of melancholy to be hot and dry, not a cold and dry distemperature, as some hold, from the heat of the brain, roasting the blood, immoderate heat of the liver and bowels, and inflammation of the Pylorus. And so much the rather, because that, as Galen holds, all spices inflame the blood, solitariness, waking, agues, study, meditation, all which heat: and therefore he concludes that this distemperature causing adventitious Melancholy, is not cold and dry, but hot and dry

1.2.5.2-r2.burton_quote: through adust blood so caused, as Mercurialis will have it, within or without the head

1.2.5.2-r3.burton_quote: will have it arise from a cold and dry distemperature of the brain

1.2.5.2-r4.burton_quote: or by vapours which arise from the other parts, and fume up into the head, altering the animal faculties

1.2.5.2-r5.burton_quote: distemperature of the heart; sometimes hot; sometimes cold

1.2.5.2-r6.burton_quote: The Liver is the shop of humours

1.2.5.2-r7.burton_quote: The Stomach, and Meseraic veins do often concur, by reason of their obstructions

1.2.5.2-r9.burton_quote: from that menstruous blood turned into melancholy, and seed too long detained (as I have already declared) by putrefaction or adustion
1.2.5.2-r9.translation: From putrefaction of the blood in the seminal vessels and the womb
